newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paribas sees second half not as strong.
newsitem.headline: Paribas sees second half not as strong.

text.p: Groupe Paribas said on Thursday it did not expect its second half to be as strong as the first but said it would exceed in 1996 its goal of a 10 percent return on equity.
"The first half results are going in the right direction," company chairman Andre Levy-Lang told a news conference.

He cautioned against using the first half results as a guide to full year prospects, noting that the bulk of capital gains had been made in the first half and that there were no big divestments expected in the second half.
An overall positive trend was continuing in the second half for banking activities globally, he said.
But he noted the latter half of the year was traditionally less active on the capital markets side, adding the first signals from July, August and September provided no reason to think otherwise.
Paribas reported a first half net attributable profit of 4.042 billion francs versus 609 million francs at the same stage last year.

The main reason for the spectacular increase was a strong performance from Banque Paribas and the unit Paribas Affaires Industrielles, with the latter registering capital gains of 2.644 billion francs versus 358 million in first-half 1995.

The big deals included a 16 percent stake in Audiofina, the stock exchange placing of 25 percent of Axime, the sale of a first tranche of Poliet and a share offer by Canal Plus to buy UGC-DA audiovisual rights company.
